replies.text:
Step 2 checks:
- Automated abuse of a reachable entry point: design states no sign-in, form, email/SMS or public API ("caches patient notes and medical history offline in a local SQLite database" is the only stated surface; deterministic signals say `"auth": false`, `"exposure":"internal"`) — not present.
- Staff/privileged screens rendering other people's content: design names only "a tablet app that caches patient notes and medical history" with no viewing of externally-supplied content or uploads (`"fileUpload": false`) — not present.
- Privileged actions with no record of who did it: present — notes written on devices "shared between shifts"; already covered by listed threat 2 (Repudiation) and threat 5.
- Personal/financial documents that caches or proxies could store: present as the local cache ("local SQLite database"); already covered by listed threats 3 and 4.
- Attacker-controlled text flowing into logs, exports, emails or another interpreter: design states no logging, export or notification path — not present.
- Single-reviewer item #2 (offline cache keeps serving records after access is revoked): real and not covered — the list covers device loss/theft and over-broad scope, but not that access decisions keep working "without signal" for a user whose account has been disabled; reporting it as the one gap. Items #1, #3, #4, #5 duplicate listed threats 5, 4, 4 and 3.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-03",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Nurse tablet app", "Local SQLite cache", "Backend sync service"],
    "dataStores": ["Local SQLite database", "Backend patient record store"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Shared tablet (offline) to backend sync"],
    "dataClasses": ["health", "pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Offline app keeps granting access to cached records after the account is revoked",
      "scenario": "A nurse who leaves, changes ward or has her account disabled keeps a shared tablet. Because the app is designed to keep working \"without signal\", access is decided locally against the cached SQLite copy, so no backend revocation reaches the device. The former staff member (or anyone to whom they hand the tablet) carries on opening patient notes and medical history for every cached patient indefinitely, and may also author notes that later sync. The design states no expiry, re-authentication on reconnect, or remote revocation of the cache.",
      "component": "Tablet app offline authorisation / local SQLite cache",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Nurses use a tablet app that caches patient notes and medical history offline in a local SQLite database so they can work without signal. Devices are shared between shifts." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V3.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613"],
      "plainLanguage": "Turning off a nurse's account does not stop the tablet: it keeps showing cached patient records because the app is built to work with no network.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Revoke offline access and expire the cached record set",
        "given": "a tablet holds a local SQLite cache of patient notes and medical history and can be used without signal",
        "when": "the signed-in nurse's account is disabled, her assignment changes, or the cache exceeds a defined offline validity window without a successful backend check-in",
        "then": "the app must refuse to open or sync cached patient records and must purge the local cache, requiring a fresh authenticated authorisation check from the backend before records are readable again"
      }
    }
  ]
}
